summary.text: 來, “come,” began as a picture of wheat according to the supplied accounts. The character was then borrowed to write a similar-sounding word meaning “come.” This explains why its shape has no obvious connection to arrival: the drawing belongs to an earlier use, while “wheat” is now written 麥.

history.text: Wiktionary describes an ear, leaves, stem and roots in the early drawing, and reports that the borrowed use for “come” already occurs in oracle-bone writing. It also describes later attempts to add a foot or walking component to distinguish uses; those additions did not survive in the usual form.

uncertainties.text: The precise early relationship between 來 and 麥 remains less secure. The supplied account also records a proposal that 麥 originally wrote “come,” with the uses subsequently switching. The Shuowen’s explanation that wheat “comes from heaven” is a historical interpretation, rather than evidence establishing that sequence.
